title: Mrs. Michal Tawil: What is wrong with this picture? (class #20)

chapters.title: Recognizing Hashem in daily situations
chapters.about: Saying I cannot do something is denying Hashem's presence; finding solutions shows faith.

chapters.title: Accepting your current level
chapters.about: A story about kidney donation and learning to accept where you are happily.

chapters.title: Climbing the steps of the Bet HaMikdash
chapters.about: King David's steps teach us to grow slowly, take short steps, and pray in between.

chapters.title: Triggers as opportunities for growth
chapters.about: Pennina's story about her husband starting kiddush and the 5-inch challenge.

chapters.title: The cardinal rule of well-being
chapters.about: We are responsible for our own well-being first and should stop expecting reciprocal perfection.

chapters.title: The name of Hashem: Misov Habot
chapters.about: Understanding Hashem as the primal cause who turns all the cogs in the world machine.

chapters.title: The pictures in our heads versus reality
chapters.about: How rigid expectations and 'shoulds' function like idol worship and block our growth.

chapters.title: Embracing surprise and God's reality
chapters.about: Learning to accept surprises as adventures rather than falling into depression or anger.

summary: Mrs. Tawil goes through how dealing with unexpected life triggers and challenges allows us to grow spiritually and connect with Hashem instead of clinging to our own rigid expectations. She discusses practical examples, such as preparing for Shabbat or handling daily disruptions, and introduces the concept of Hashem as Misov Habot, the primal cause of all reality.
questions: How should we react when our plans or expectations do not match reality?
What does it mean to accept our current spiritual level instead of constantly tormenting ourselves?
How does the structure of the steps leading up to the Bet HaMikdash teach us about personal growth?
What is the danger of living according to the 'shoulds' and pictures we create in our heads?
How can daily triggers and stress serve as opportunities to draw closer to Hashem?
